turn.student: כמה זמן אפשר לשמור ביצים במקרר?

turns.text:
המסמך שלנו לא מציין כמה זמן בדיוק אפשר לשמור ביצים (זה מעבר למה שכתוב במסמך, אבל באופן כללי ביצים נשמרות במקרר שבועות ספורים). 

בוא נחזור לשאלה שלנו על הלחם: יצורים זעירים ממש ממש קטנים שחיים סביבנו מתיישבים על הלחם [c1]. 

מה לדעתך קורה ללחם שגורם להופעת אותם כתמים ירוקים אחרי כמה ימים בשקית?

turn.student: Magnets attract only a few materials. Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are pulled by a magnet. Most other materials, including many metals such as aluminium, copper, gold and silver, are not attracted at all.

conceptsShown: magnets attract only a few materials

turns.text: Those are the exact words from the text! To show you've got it, try explaining it in your own words, just like you would tell a friend: In a recycling plant, a big magnet separates steel cans from aluminium cans. How can it do that?

turn.student: The steel cans have iron in them so the magnet grabs them, and aluminium just isn't a magnetic metal, so those cans are left.

conceptsShown: steel contains iron and is attracted by magnets
aluminium is not attracted by magnets

turns.text:
Spot on—steel contains iron so the magnet grabs it, while aluminium is left behind because it is not attracted to magnets. 

Now let's look at how magnets help us navigate! Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet [c4]. A compass contains a small, light magnet for a needle that can spin around freely [c4]. Just like two bar magnets interacting, Earth's invisible magnetic forces pull on the compass needle to line it up from north to south [c4]. 

Why does a compass needle always point north?

turn.student: Because in December Australia is closer to the Sun than Europe is.

label.misconception: seasons come from distance to the Sun

turns.misconception: Thinking that summer in Australia is caused by being closer to the Sun.

conceptsMissing: opposite seasons show distance is not the cause

turns.text:
Let's check how the Sun warms our planet first. When your half of the Earth is tilted toward the Sun, sunlight hits the ground straight down like a bright flashlight, making it warmer [c2]. When it is tilted away, the light arrives at a slant and spreads out, so it is cooler [c2]. 

When your half of the Earth is having summer, is it tilted toward or away from the Sun?
